title: Visual Fallback Orchestrator — Console Policy Editor Flow
creator: Aisha Reynolds
description:
Background: Customers increasingly ask for an end-to-end UI that lets non-SRE product teams author routing policies that cover region selection, tiered routing (e.g. paid vs free tiers), and deterministic fallback model variants when capacity or SLAs degrade. Current console flows expose low-level route definitions and a separate simulator; users tell us this is confusing and error-prone for multi-dimensional policies.

Goal: Ship a 'Visual Fallback Orchestrator' panel in the Console Policy Editor that lets customers: (1) visually compose region + tier routing rules, (2) declare ordered fallback model variants with constraints, (3) run quick validations and traffic previews against synthetic and sample real telemetry, and (4) receive safety/linting suggestions for availability/cost tradeoffs. The flow should be approachable for PMs and platform owners while allowing advanced users to edit the underlying DSL.
acceptance_criteria:
1) Policy editor contains a new "Visual Fallback Orchestrator" tab with a canvas that allows drag-and-drop of regions and tiers.
2) Users can add fallback chains for each route (primary model -> variant A -> variant B) and configure conditions (latency threshold, error rate, cost cap).
3) Validation engine surfaces warnings and errors inline; sample validations for at least three real-world scenarios (region outage, capacity saturation, high tail latency) included.
4) Preview mode simulates 1k synthetic requests and shows distribution of traffic across regions/tiers/variants, with estimated cost and avg/95th latency.
5) Advanced toggle shows the generated DSL and allows save-only-if-dsl-unchanged flow.
6) Unit tests for validation rules and e2e test for preview runner are present and passing.
implementation_notes:
Front-end: new tab and canvas component in Console (React + Typescript). Reuse existing rule editor components where possible to keep parity. Back-end: extend policy validation service with three new constraint checks (region-affinity cycles, tier-safety cost cap, fallback-compatibility across model families). Preview runner will call a sandboxed simulation service (ENG-4920) which accepts policy snapshot and traffic profile. Add telemetry hooks to capture preview delta metrics for later QA.

APIs: PATCH/PUT to /policies/:id with an optional ?validateOnly flag. New endpoint POST /policies/:id/preview to run simulation. Ensure auth respects dedicated/private deployment contexts.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (Beta): Internal-only for 2 customers and Redwood internal infra; collect UX feedback and failure modes. Phase 2 (Limited Beta): Invite customers on Dedicated tiers and 10 early enrollments. Phase 3 (General Availability): Wide release with migration doc and training webinar. Feature flag gated by console.feature.visualFallbackOrchestrator.
testing_plan:
- Unit tests for UI components and validation rules.
- Integration test for policy save + DSL roundtrip.
- E2E: preview runner simulates three failure scenarios and assertions on distribution/cost.
- Manual: run with a staging Dedicated tenant, compare preview estimates to small-scale canary traffic.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Preview estimates diverge from real traffic leading to trust erosion. Mitigation: show confidence intervals, surface sampling methodology, and label estimates as "approximate". Risk: Complex policies may create cycles causing routing loops. Mitigation: validation rule rejects cycles and provides an auto-suggested fix. Risk: Exposing model variant metadata could leak internal model names. Mitigation: UI masks internal-only variant IDs for customers on shared hosted tier.
